# S229 — Daemon and engine wording leftovers from the TUI notes

Seven small fixes in `internal/daemon` and `internal/engine` that the TUI notes sweep (S190) could not hold: the blocked-wave refusal text, the spec-check directory of a commit-stopped run, the error mapping and wording for an unreadable `run.json`, and the renders error wording on the approval card.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-01** — Open owner questions from the 2026-10-31 spec drafting (drafter F). The spec is written for option (a) in both; neither blocks the implementer, but the owner may change them before the relay starts. Q1: exact wording of the blocked refusal, the unreadable-record message and the renders error; recommended as drafted. Q2: remove the spec-check directory when the merge is found (recommended, option a) or only at run cleanup (option b).

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Three later-notes rows each hold items that need a daemon or engine file, so they cannot sit in an N-class TUI sweep (the rule at `docs/design.md`, search "at most one slice whose Files touch"). The owner decided on 2026-10-31 that later-notes rows are folded into sweep slices and the folded rows are retired once the sweep is filed. This slice carries the daemon and engine half of those rows. S186, S191 and S201 are retired once this slice is filed; their other items go to the TUI notes sweep (S190) or were dropped there. This slice is E-class and pairs with an N-class slice in a later wave (owner, 2026-10-31: pair waves).

The items, each re-anchored at HEAD `2b6a27a`:

- S186 item 1: a blocker shared by several items repeats its quoted title each time. `BlockedMessage` (`internal/daemon/build.go:72-112`) names the title for every `waits on` entry. Show it the first time only; later mentions use the id and the reason.
- S186 item 2: `untick S182, S183 or land S181, S175 first` reads ambiguously (`build.go:107-110`). Write `untick S182 and S183, or land S181 and S175 first`.
- S186 item 3: the title uses `%q` (`build.go:91`), so a title with a double quote shows a backslash. Quote it plainly.
- S191 item 2: the spec-check directory of a run stopped after commit is removed only when the run lands. Cleanup is keyed on `LandedAt` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:218-222,888-890`). A commit-stopped run never lands through ork; the owner merges its branch, and `checkMerged` (`internal/daemon/landed.go:102-165`) finds that out. The directory stays until the 14-day sweep sees the item done (`internal/daemon/speccheck_state.go:119-171`). Remove it when the merge is found.
- S201 item 2: `loadFinishedEngine` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1124-1137`) maps every `Store.Open` error to `not_found` `no run ID`. A run whose `run.json` exists and cannot be read is not "no run"; `openRun` (`runs.go:1376-1388`, S147) already says so for `run.report` and `run.render`. Use `openRun` here too.
- S201 item 3: no test pins `openRun` for a `run.json` of an unknown version (`internal/runrec/store.go:135-137` returns it as an error that is neither `ErrBadRunID` nor not-exist, so it takes the unreadable branch). Add the test.
- S201 item 4: the viewer error for an unreadable `run.json` repeats itself and shows the absolute path: `Could not read NAME: internal: run X cannot be read: run record /abs/path/run.json: ...`. The card's `readReason` (`internal/engine/approval.go:238-246`) gives the cause without the path. Do the same in `openRun`. The `Could not read NAME:` and `internal:` parts are TUI text (`internal/tui/report.go:143`, `internal/tui/model.go:1677-1687`) and stay as they are.
- S201 item 5: the card says `not the listed file` for a swapped link (`internal/engine/approval.go:309`), which is internal wording, and chains two colons (`could not be read: b.txt: permission denied`, built at `approval.go:275` and shown by `internal/tui/card.go:138-142`). Say `replaced while being read` and write `b.txt (permission denied)`.

These changes are small wording and cleanup changes. The merge cleanup (S191 item 2) is *proposed* until an adj record decides it. The seven items are not an adj decision; the wording choices below are this spec's text for the owner to review.

Not in this slice: S186 item 4 (the 80-column test; it is a TUI test, built in the TUI notes sweep), S191's other items, S201 item 1 (report viewer order; TUI), and any change to `internal/tui`. The TUI tests that hold the old refusal text as a fixture (`internal/tui/waves_test.go:1485,1497`, `internal/cli/wave_test.go:409`) inject the message and do not compute it, so they keep passing; leave them alone so a paired N-class slice does not conflict.

## Failing tests

Each test is Go, stdlib only, in the style of its neighbours. "Fails first" names the reason the test is red before the change.

Refusal text (`internal/daemon/wave_test.go`):

- `TestBlockedMessageNamesASharedBlockerTitleOnce`: call `BlockedMessage([]string{"S2","S3"}, deps, map[string]string{"S9":"Prior"})` with S2 and S3 both blocked by S9. Want exactly `S2 waits on S9 "Prior" (not done); S3 waits on S9 (not done); land S9 first`. Fails first: the second entry repeats `"Prior"`.
- `TestBlockedMessageJoinsNamesWithAnd`: table, titles empty. (a) ids S182 and S183; S182 blocked by S181; S183 blocked by S182 and S175. Want `S182 waits on S181 (not done); S183 waits on S182 (in this wave, not done), S175 (not done); untick S182 and S183, or land S181, S182 and S175 first`. (b) one in-wave blocker: ids S1 and S2, S2 blocked by S1. Want `S2 waits on S1 (in this wave, not done); untick S2, or land S1 first`. (c) two blockers outside the wave: want `land S9 and S8 first`. Fails first: the lists join with commas and `or` has no comma.
- `TestBlockedMessageShowsATitleWithAQuoteAsIs`: title `The "big" one` gives `S2 waits on S9 "The "big" one" (not done); land S9 first`. A second title with a CSI escape and a newline, `a\x1b[31mb\nc`, gives `"ab c"` (control characters dropped, whitespace collapsed). Fails first: `%q` writes `\"` and escapes.
- Existing tests whose expected text changes, same names: `TestWaveStartNamesABlockerInTheSameWave` (`untick S2, or land S1 first`), `TestWaveStartPreservesDependencyOrderAndReadsEachItemOnce` (`...; untick S3 and S2, or land S9, S2 and S1 first`), `TestBlockedMessageShowsTitlesAndTheNextStep` and `TestBlockedMessageFallsBackToTheIdWhenATitleReadFails` (`land S9 and S8 first`), `TestWaveStartRefusesACycleInsideOneWave` (`untick S2 and S1, or land S1 and S2 first`). They fail first for the same reasons. `TestWaveStartRefusesABlockedItem` and `TestBlockerTitlesAreReadOncePerDistinctBlocker` keep passing.

Commit-stopped cleanup (`internal/daemon/landed_test.go`):

- `TestMergedCommitStoppedRunDropsItsSpecCheckDir`: `landingDaemon(t, 0, "")`, `committedRun(t, s, p, "run", "committed")` (item S63, no `LandedAt`). Write `d.specDir(p.Name, "S63")/answers.json` with `writeSpecJSON` and put an entry in `d.runs.specs[specKey(p.Name, "S63")]`. `refreshHead`. Want the directory gone and the entry gone. Fails first: nothing removes it.
- `TestUnmergedOrUnknownCommitStoppedRunKeepsItsSpecCheckDir`: the same with exit 1 (not merged) and exit 2 (git error, merge state unknown). Want the directory and the entry kept. Passes on arrival; it pins the guard.
- `TestMergeCheckSpecCleanupDoesNotWaitForSpecMu`: the exit 0 case run through `assertSpecMuDoesNotBlock(t, d, func() error { return d.cache.Refresh(ctx, p, source.Head) })` (`internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go:737`). Passes on arrival if the lock order is right (`specStateMu` before `mu`).

Unreadable records (`internal/daemon/render_test.go`, `internal/daemon/file_test.go`):

- `TestRunRenderSaysWhenTheRecordIsUnreadable` (existing): change the wanted message to start `the record of run bad is unreadable: `, to contain `invalid character`, and to not contain `store.RunDir("bad")` and not `cannot be read`. Keep the `nope` and `../r1` not-found checks. Fails first: the message is `run bad cannot be read: run record /abs/.../run.json: ...`.
- `TestOpenRunSaysWhichVersionARecordHas`: a run with `run.json` rewritten to `{"version":N}` where N is `runrec.Version+1`; `run.report` and `run.render` both give code `internal` and the message `the record of run bad is unreadable: unknown version N (this ork reads version 1)` (build the text with `fmt.Sprintf` from `runrec.Version`). Fails first: the old wording and path. This also covers S201 item 3.
- `TestUnreadableRecordIsNotNoRunForAFinishedRunAction`: three runs: `bad` (committed record, `run.json` overwritten with `{not json`), `ver` (version N), `ok` (committed, one later finding). `d.handle(ctx, "run.file", {"run":"bad","finding":1})` gives code `internal` and a message that starts `the record of run bad is unreadable: `; the same for `ver`. `nope` and `../x` give `not_found` and `no run nope` / `no run ../x`. Fails first: `bad` and `ver` give `not_found` `no run bad`.
- A mode-0 sub-case: `run.json` with mode 0 gives `the record of run bad is unreadable: permission denied`. Use the skip-when-readable pattern of `TestCardSaysWhyRendersCouldNotBeRead` (`internal/engine/renders_test.go:417-428`).

Renders error wording (`internal/engine/renders_test.go`):

- `TestCardSaysWhyRendersCouldNotBeRead` (existing): add a `wantReason` string to the table and compare with `==`: `permission denied` for `a directory with mode 0`, `b-80x24.txt (permission denied)` for `a file with mode 0`. Fails first: the file case gives `b-80x24.txt: permission denied`.
- `TestSwappedRenderErrorHasNoInternalWording`: `errNotThatFile.Error()` is `replaced while being read`, and `TestReadRenderRefusesAFileSwappedForALink` (`:285`) still passes with `errors.Is(err, errNotThatFile)`. Fails first: the text is `not the listed file`.

## Implement

Tests first (write the failing tests above, run them, see them red for the stated reason), then:

1. `internal/daemon/build.go` `BlockedMessage`. (a) Keep a `titled` set. When a blocker's title is non-empty and not yet in the set, write `ID "TITLE"` and add it; otherwise write the id alone. A title is `strings.Join(strings.Fields(runrec.PlainText(title)), " ")` inside plain double quotes, with no `%q`. If that is empty, the id alone. `runrec` is already imported by the daemon package; add the import to `build.go`. (b) Add a small helper `joinAnd(names []string) string`: one name as is, two as `A and B`, more as `A, B and C`. (c) Next step: `land ` + `joinAnd(blockerIDs)` + ` first`; when a blocker is in the wave, `untick ` + `joinAnd(blockedIDs)` + `, or ` + the land text. Keep the order and the dedupe of ids as they are. Do not change `EngineConflict` or the entry text `ID waits on ... (not done)`.
2. `internal/daemon/landed.go` `checkMerged`. In the write-back under `d.runs.mu` (the loop over `results`, `:151-159`), before `d.runs.merged[id] = merged`, note each run whose new value is true and whose previous value was nil or false. Keep its project and item (from `records`). After `d.runs.mu.Unlock()` and before `d.changed`, take `d.runs.specStateMu` then `d.runs.mu` (the order used at `runs.go:218-222`) and call `d.removeSpecDirLocked(project, item)` for each noted run; unlock both. Do not hold `specStateMu` while git runs. A run that is not merged, or whose merge state is unknown, removes nothing. After a daemon restart `merged` starts empty, so the first HEAD check removes the directory of an already merged run. Do not change `recoverRuns`, `launchRun`, `sweepSpecDirs` or `removeSpecDirLocked`.
3. `internal/daemon/runs.go` `openRun`. Replace the final `fmt.Errorf("run %s cannot be read: %w", id, err)` with an error whose text is `the record of run ID is unreadable: CAUSE`. CAUSE is `pe.Err.Error()` when `errors.As(err, &pe)` finds an `*fs.PathError` (for example `permission denied`), otherwise `err.Error()` with the leading `run record ` + path + `: ` removed, where the path is `filepath.Join(d.runs.deps.Store.RunDir(id), "run.json")`; if the prefix is not there, use `err.Error()` with every occurrence of the run directory plus a separator removed, so no absolute path remains. Keep `%w` wrapping so `errors.Is` still sees the cause. Update the doc comment above `openRun`.
4. `internal/daemon/runs.go` `loadFinishedEngine`. Replace `d.runs.deps.Store.Open(id)` and its blanket `not_found` with `d.openRun(id)`. Keep the `no run engine for ID` and `d.registered` branches as they are.
5. `internal/engine/approval.go`. Set `errNotThatFile = errors.New("replaced while being read")` (`:309`; keep the identifier). In `uiRenders` (`:275`) write `ent.Name() + " (" + readReason(err) + ")"`. Leave the directory case (`readErr = readReason(err)`) as it is.
6. Docs. `docs/design.md`: the `renders_error` sentence (`:627`) says a file reads as `NAME (WHY)`; the unreadable-record sentence (`:1288`) says the message `the record of run ID is unreadable: WHY`, without the path. `docs/state.md`: add `or when a run stopped after commit is found merged` to the removal sentence (`:178-179`), marked *proposed*; add the `NAME (WHY)` form to the `renders_error` sentence (`:354-357`). `docs/dashboard.md`: the refusal example becomes `S2 waits on S1 "Title" (in this wave, not done); untick S2, or land S1 first`, and add one sentence that a blocker shared by several items shows its title the first time only; the `WHY` of the Renders line reads `NAME (WHY)` for a single file. Mark the merge cleanup *proposed* where it is described.
7. Do NOT touch `internal/tui`, `internal/cli`, golden views, `internal/runrec`, `internal/daemon/speccheck_state.go`, or the TUI/CLI tests that hold the old refusal text as a fixture. Do not add a wire code. Do not restart the daemon or touch `~/bin/ork`.
8. Add the CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`, as one new bullet at the end of that section, so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict. Text (one entry): the blocked-wave refusal shows a shared blocker's title once, joins names with `and`, and quotes a title plainly; a run stopped after commit drops its spec-check directory when its branch is found merged (*proposed*); an unreadable `run.json` is an `internal` error without the path for finding actions too, and its message no longer repeats itself; the renders error names a file as `NAME (WHY)` and says `replaced while being read`. Name S186, S191 and S201 as the rows it closes.
9. Run the checks. Then finish with the UI pass: UI slice: UI pass (r14).
